description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:225 — RESERVED_SET_ERROR_WIRE_NAMES is
declared `pub const` with a hand-maintained list of 8 wire-name strings.

The constant is intended as the source of truth for the debug_assert in
`with_extra`. Making it `pub` was justified at the time as "consumers
can reference the same list — e.g. a future contract test, or a
wire-format conformance check" (per the comment on the constant).

The contract problem: once `pub`, the constant's value becomes part of
the API surface. Adding a new typed field to SetError (say
`maxKeywords` for a hypothetical RFC 8621 errata) requires appending
the new wire-name to the constant. Any consumer that did one of the
following silently breaks:

- Iterates the constant and assumes its length is stable
  (`for name in RESERVED_SET_ERROR_WIRE_NAMES { … }` with a fixed
  expectation about iteration count).
- Pattern-matches against the constant's individual strings (e.g. a
  consumer's own wire-shape test that hard-codes the same 8 names).
- Treats the constant as a closed enumeration of "wire fields a
  consumer's extra-injection logic should avoid" — a new typed field
  later makes a previously-valid `with_extra(name, …)` call newly
  invalid.

What callers cannot depend on: that any of the above stay working
across additions to the constant. Additions are non-breaking by the
type system but are breaking for consumers that lean on the value.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is: the kit cannot grow SetError
typed fields without minor-version bumps that silently break consumer
contract assumptions; or the constant freezes and new typed fields
have to ship under a different mechanism.

Resolution: make the constant `pub(crate)`. The runtime debug_assert
on `with_extra` already implements the consumer-facing contract
("you cannot pass these strings"); consumers do not need direct
read access. The test
`reserved_set_error_wire_names_matches_serialized_surface` lives
in the same crate and uses the constant directly without needing
public visibility.

If a future consumer use case genuinely requires the public list,
ship it through a stable function (`is_reserved_wire_name(&str) ->
bool`) so the kit retains additive freedom.
title: RESERVED_SET_ERROR_WIRE_NAMES pub const locks consumer assumptions about typed-field set
